case_context.legal_issue: Whether the refusal to grant a loudspeaker permit impeded the petitioner's fundamental right to freedom of peaceful assembly under Article 14(1)(b) of the Constitution.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that the denial of the permit hindered his ability to hold a peaceful public meeting, thus violating his right to freedom of peaceful assembly.
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents argued that the refusal was necessary to prevent a breach of the peace due to competing meetings on the same day and location, thus justifying restrictions on assembly rights.
key_facts: Petitioner sought to hold a public meeting with loudspeaker use on 9 May 1992.
Another political meeting was scheduled on the same day and venue by a rival party.
The police refused the permit citing risk of breach of peace.
Petitioner was not properly informed or consulted in a timely manner.
The police inquiry into neighborhood inconvenience was one-sided, focusing only on the petitioner's meeting.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court emphasized that freedom of peaceful assembly includes the right to hold public meetings with necessary means such as loudspeakers. Restrictions must be reasonable and not arbitrary. The failure to properly handle the petitioner's application and the pretextual rival application undermined the petitioner's right to assemble peacefully.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the respondents' conduct was unreasonable and that the refusal to grant the permit was not justified by genuine public order concerns, thus violating the petitioner's right to peaceful assembly.
principles_established: Freedom of peaceful assembly includes the right to hold public meetings with amplification.
Restrictions on assembly must be justified and not arbitrary or discriminatory.
Authorities must act fairly and transparently when managing competing assembly requests.

outcome.holding: The court held that the denial of the loudspeaker permit violated the petitioner's fundamental right to freedom of peaceful assembly under Article 14(1)(b) and awarded compensation and costs.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: The 1st and 2nd respondents were ordered to pay compensation and costs to the petitioner.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 14(1)(b) protects the right to freedom of peaceful assembly, which was directly impacted by the refusal to grant a permit necessary for the petitioner to hold a public meeting peacefully.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: By denying the petitioner a permit for loudspeakers to enable him to hold a public meeting the petitioner’s fundamental right of the freedom of speech enshrined in Article 14(1)(a) and (b) of the Constitution is violated.
